notes: selfhost has no Copilot hook, so nothing covers what these rules miss.
Copilot treats any managed permission rule as a policy: once one is set, every operation no rule matches asks for approval.

The .github-private copy reaches only users who get their Copilot license from the enterprise; the file-based copy applies on the machine, and Copilot CLI on macOS and Linux reads it only when root owns it and it is not group- or world-writable.
Not checked against a Copilot Business or Enterprise organization.

rules.detail: Shell rules cover every command the regular expression matches.
Shell(git reset --hard *) matches whole words, so git reset --hard followed by more characters is missed. Nothing checks the rest on Copilot.
Shell(...) matches a command prefix or the exact text, and rm -rf has no ^ before it. Nothing checks it on Copilot.
Copilot's Shell(...) rules match a prefix or exact text, and the regular expression uses quantifier .*. Nothing checks it on Copilot.
In Copilot's rules / is the workspace root, as selfhost reads paths from the repository root.
Edit is another agent's tool name: Copilot reports this tool as create or edit.
Domain(*.pastebin.com) covers the subdomains, and also pastebin.com itself.
Observe mode: nothing native is written until the rule is enforced. Copilot's managed rules cover shell commands, file paths and domains, not tools by name. Nothing checks it on Copilot.
The rule is only for Codex.
allowedMcpServers blocks every other server name. Like selfhost, it trusts the name the user gave the server.
Observe mode: nothing native is written until the rule is enforced. Copilot's managed settings pick a default model and have no allow list. Nothing checks it on Copilot.
